units.uncovered_note: Students are confused by inconsistent course AI policies across courses.

units.passage: Am I adopting a policy that aligns with the norms and standards of my discipline, college, department, and/or program?
units.why: "Am I adopting a policy that aligns with the norms and standards of my discipline, college, department, and/or program?" asks instructors to align with disciplinary and unit norms; no type fits (P83 is about learning objectives, P85 about units setting their own rules), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors should check that their AI policy fits discipline, college, department or program norms.

units.passage: While mixed results have been shown with respect to honor pledges at the course level, these are an additional option to consider.
units.why: "Honor pledges ... are an additional option to consider" offers an honor pledge as a course device; it matches none of the types, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors may use a course-level honor pledge.

units.passage: Look for opportunities to check in with students’ processes and learning strategies.
units.why: "Look for opportunities to check in with students' processes and learning strategies" advises process check-ins. No type covers process check-ins as such (P34 is code reviews or oral exams to verify understanding; P35 is assignment redesign), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Instructors are advised to check in on students' processes and learning strategies as an AI-era teaching practice; not verification of understanding or assignment redesign.

units.passage: The moment a DePaul student, faculty, or staff member considers creating a new technology service that interacts with other people in the DePaul community, this service must undergo a thorough design, security, and data review like any other product that is used in our technological environment.
units.why: Any AI-based app or service that 'interacts with any other members of the DePaul community' must 'undergo a thorough design, security, and data review'. No type covers review of AI-built services, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Required design, security and data review before an AI-based app or service is offered to other members of the university community.

units.passage: Assuming no protected data has been used, it is possible to build apps or tools for professional use if they are strictly used by the individual and not shared. Once an app or tool is shared with others, it requires a thorough review like any other technology application
units.why: Vibe-coding or app-building is allowed 'for professional use if they are strictly used by the individual and not shared', with sharing requiring review. It is a conditional permission on AI-built apps that fits no coursework type, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Conditional permission to build apps with AI/vibe-coding tools when used only individually, with no protected data, and not shared.

units.passage: Once an app or tool is shared with others, it requires a thorough review like any other technology application or service employed by the university.
units.why: 'Once an app or tool is shared with others, it requires a thorough review like any other technology application' extends the review requirement to shared AI-built apps. No type covers review of AI-built tools (P65 is vendor agreements), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: AI-built apps or tools shared with others require a thorough review like any other university technology service.

units.passage: AI-based apps or tools created independently should never appear to be created or endorsed by the university, and the use of university tools to generate personal profit is prohibited.
units.why: 'the use of university tools to generate personal profit is prohibited' and AI-built apps must not appear university-endorsed; a restriction on AI-built tools, not a type in the list, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: AI-built apps must not appear created or endorsed by the university, and university tools may not be used for personal profit.

units.passage: ITCS Information Security Best Practices must be followed and any suspicious messages reported to phish@ecu.edu
units.why: Says generative AI is 'a prominent driver of phishing scams' and requires following security practices and reporting. AI-enabled security threats fit no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: AI-enabled phishing and information-security practices: follow ITCS best practices and report suspicious messages (cybersecurity, not data privacy or bias).

units.passage: Pol icy ETSU recognizes the potential benefits of the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies (AIT), including Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), by faculty, staff, and students for instructional and assignment purposes , but is also aware of its limitations and the potential risks. The use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies, in cluding GAI, to fabricate data or research results, or to falsify academic content is strictly prohibited.
units.why: Using AI 'to fabricate data or research results, or to falsify academic content is strictly prohibited'; a flat ban on a specific misuse that none of the closed types covers (it is not P19, which is about submitting AI-made work as one's own).
units.uncovered_note: Strict ban on using AI to fabricate data or research results or falsify academic content.

units.passage: Misuse, including falsifying academic content or research data or ﬁndings, generating malicious or misleading information, or infringing on intellectual property rights, is strictly prohibited.
units.policy: Misuse, including falsifying academic content or research data or findings, generating malicious or misleading information, or infringing on intellectual property rights, is strictly prohibited.
units.why: 'Misuse, including falsifying academic content or research data ..., generating malicious or misleading information, or infringing on intellectual property rights, is strictly prohibited'; a ban on named misuses that no closed type captures.
units.uncovered_note: Strict ban on misuse: falsifying academic content or research data, generating malicious or misleading information, infringing intellectual property.

units.passage: Staying Current and Informed University Aﬃliates who employ generative artiﬁcial intelligence technologies shall maintain ongoing awareness of developments, best practices, and emerging guidelines in Gen AI.
units.why: Affiliates 'shall maintain ongoing awareness of developments, best practices, and emerging guidelines'; a duty to keep up with AI that no closed type names exactly.
units.uncovered_note: Users must keep up to date with developments, best practices and guidelines on generative AI (Core Principle 4).

units.passage: Regularly review available university resources to remain current on best practices for responsible AI use.
units.why: Students should 'regularly review available university resources to remain current on best practices'; the same keep-up duty as Core Principle 4 applied to students.
units.uncovered_note: Students review university resources to stay current on responsible AI use.

units.passage: Regularly consult institutional support materials and engage in institutional training to stay informed about emerging Gen AI practices relevant to instruction, assessment, and academic integrity. (Core Principle 4) 3. Researchers (Data Collection, Analysis Use, & Creative Activities) a. Transparent Disclosure: Clearly disclose the speciﬁc generative AI tools used, their purpose, and methods of application within the Methods or Acknowledgments sections of research publications. AI should never be credited as an author nor used as a sole, undisclosed generator of creative works. (Core Principle 1) b. Protect Participant Data: Secure IRB approval and informed consent before utilizing generative AI to analyze any human-subject data. All personal identiﬁers must be removed prior to analysis or AI-based processing. (Core Principle 2) c. Bias and Accuracy Checks: Document all bias checks and veriﬁcation procedures in lab notebooks or in public registries, such as the Open Science Framework (OSF), to transparently communicate limitations and maintain research integrity. (Core Principle 3) d. Continuous Learning: Regularly consult institutional support materials and participate in research-focused AI training, workshops, or seminars provided by the Oﬃce of Research and Sponsored Programs (ORSP) to remain up to date with ethical standards and best practices.
units.why: Researchers should participate in 'research-focused AI training, workshops, or seminars' to stay current; the same keep-up duty as Core Principle 4.
units.uncovered_note: Researchers regularly consult materials and take AI training to stay up to date with ethical standards and practices.

units.passage: Stay updated with institutional training and workshops to eﬀectively integrate responsible AI use into administrative tasks, ensuring alignment with university policies and ethical standards.
units.why: Staff should 'Stay updated with institutional training and workshops' to integrate AI in administrative tasks; the keep-up duty of Core Principle 4 for staff.
units.uncovered_note: Staff keep up with institutional training to integrate responsible AI use into administrative tasks.

units.passage: Emphasize learning and fairness over punishment, and try to keep the tone warm.
units.why: Instructors should 'Emphasize learning and fairness over punishment, and try to keep the tone warm'; a tone/approach for responding to misuse that no closed type names.
units.uncovered_note: Responses to AI misuse should emphasize learning and fairness over punishment and keep a warm tone.

units.passage: “Humanize” text to circumvent GenAI detection software. Use of tools such as Humanize AI, Write Human, Undetectable AI, etc. is not permissible
units.why: Yellow bans tools that 'humanize' text to circumvent detection software: evasion of detection, no type fits.
units.uncovered_note: Ban on using humanizer tools to evade AI detection software.

units.passage: Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions to exchange knowledge, share best practices, and stay abreast of emerging trends in AI technology and policy.
units.why: Item 6b says to "Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions" to share AI practices; no type covers partnerships for knowledge exchange (P65 is about contracts and data sharing), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Institutional partnerships with industry, government and other universities to exchange AI knowledge and best practices.

units.passage: Engage students, faculty, staff, and the broader community in discussions and forums on AI ethics, privacy, and societal implications.
units.why: Item 7 engages students and staff in "discussions and forums on AI ethics, privacy, and societal implications"; it is community outreach with no matching type (P54 is policy revision), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Hold community discussions and forums on AI ethics, privacy and societal implications.

units.passage: Despite appearances, AI models including LLMs, do not possess the independent thought or the self-awareness of humans.
units.why: 'AI models including LLMs, do not possess the independent thought or the self-awareness of humans' is a fact about AI not being sentient; no type covers it.
units.fit_note: Only a limitation statement; does not discuss authorship or citation.
units.uncovered_note: States that AI is not sentient and has no independent thought.

units.passage: 3. You must sign the AI contract that you understand and agree to these policies.
units.why: "You must sign the AI contract that you understand and agree to these policies" requires a signed agreement. No type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Students must sign an AI contract acknowledging they understand and agree to the AI policy.

units.passage: Offer resources and training to support responsible use of AI for graduate students.
units.why: UGS must "Offer resources and training to support responsible use of AI for graduate students". This is student-facing, so not P63 (faculty); UNCOVERED. Consensus coding after reconciliation: unit_stance=neutral.
units.uncovered_note: University office provides resources and training to students on responsible AI use.

units.passage: Supporting data analysis with proper oversight.
units.why: Acceptable: "Supporting data analysis with proper oversight". No permitted-use type covers data analysis, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: AI may support data analysis with proper oversight.

units.passage: Consult human experts: Faculty mentors, librarians, statisticians, and colleagues remain essential.
units.why: "Consult human experts: Faculty mentors, librarians, statisticians, and colleagues remain essential" advises consulting people; P10 is about permission questions, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Students should consult human experts (mentors, librarians, statisticians, colleagues) alongside AI.

units.passage: Use domain-specific models when possible: Tools tailored to the field may reduce errors.
units.why: "Use domain-specific models when possible" is tool-choice advice that fits no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Students use domain-specific AI models when possible to reduce errors.

units.passage: It is always a best practice to prioritize proposed sanctions that educate and remediate, not merely penalize.
units.policy: Instructors prioritize proposed sanctions that educate and remediate, not merely penalize.
units.why: 'prioritize proposed sanctions that educate and remediate, not merely penalize' states a sanction principle but no concrete penalty and not classification as misconduct, so no existing type fits.
units.uncovered_note: Sanction philosophy: prefer educative and remedial sanctions over purely punitive ones.

units.passage: Do not use AI for any activity that could compromise university systems or networks, including hacking, breaching security measures, or exploiting vulnerabilities
units.why: 'Do not use AI for any activity that could compromise university systems' is a security prohibition; no type covers security misuse, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI for hacking, breaching security or exploiting vulnerabilities (security misuse), not about learning or integrity.

units.passage: Do not use AI to create or distribute malicious content, including malware, viruses, phishing emails, or any other content designed to harm individuals, systems, or networks
units.why: 'Do not use AI to create or distribute malicious content, including malware, viruses, phishing emails' is a harmful-content ban not in any type.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to create malware, phishing or other harmful content.

units.passage: Do not use AI to create or distribute malicious content, including malware, viruses, phishing emails, or any other content designed to harm individuals, systems, or networks. Such uses are prohibited under University Policy Number 1301 on the responsible use of computing. Intellectual Property Infringement: Do not use AI to create or distribute content that violates copyright or intellectual property laws per University Policy Number 1104 on copyrighted materials. Be aware that the use of AI-generated images in official university materials and any AI-generated materials produced using university resources currently bear high intellectual property risks and could expose the university to liability. Deception and Misinformation: Do not use AI to deceive others
units.why: 'Do not use AI to deceive others' including fake news and fabricated messages; a deception prohibition with no fitting type, UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Prohibition on using AI to deceive others or create false communication.
